idiom_name: SQLite.swift Table("users") + Expression<T> typed queries (GRDB as the alternative)
implementation_notes: Because the Swift standard library has no database support, the gateway comes from a package: SQLite.swift's `let users = Table("users")` with typed `Expression<Int64>` columns gives per-table insert/update/delete/filter operations whose rows are `Row` values addressable by column - the records - while `db.prepare(sql)` exposes the raw SQLite3 statement API for statement-level control. GRDB offers the same shape with Record/FetchableRecord types over its database queue. The classic structure is realized by one type or constant per table plus a thin function layer; hand-writing over the C API (`sqlite3_prepare_v2`/`sqlite3_step`) is justified only when a dependency is unacceptable or statement control is required.
pitfalls: SQLite.Expression must be qualified when SwiftUI is imported, because SwiftUI exports its own Expression type.
Row lookups are optional-typed; reading a non-null column without unwrapping or with the wrong generic type traps at runtime instead of returning an error.
One Connection is not thread-safe - share it through a serial queue / database queue, or open a connection per thread.
Skipping `try`/error handling around db.run silently loses writes in code that uses optional chaining on the throwing call.
